cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Congratulations on becoming club president. Here are the toilet keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought the caretaker cleaned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We voted to save that fee. The minutes assign closing and cleaning to the president.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and I cleaned them all year. Your first presidential duty is continuing your savings.

mechanism: A acts as the final interpreter of an existing allocation rule, proving that B unwanted task follows from the rotation or decision B previously supported.
confusable: D175 appoints a new ceremonial duty; D173 must demonstrate an already applicable rule rather than simply manufacture a title to recruit B.
comparison: Household rota uses a mutually limited swap; outgoing club president enforces a cost-saving decision against its proposer now in office.
seedUse: All four canonical seeds read. Preserve actual reciprocal swap history and enacted club minutes, distinguishing rule proof from merely declaring rank.
